subject: english
title: Food and Nutrition
summary: Vocabulary about food, healthy eating habits, the food pyramid, writing recipes, and using conditional sentences

sections.title: Talking About Food
sections.content: Students learn vocabulary related to food groups: carbohydrates (rice, bread, potatoes), proteins (fish, meat, eggs, lentils), dairy (milk, yogurt, cheese), fruits and vegetables, and fats and oils. They practice describing foods using taste words (sweet, sour, bitter, salty, spicy) and texture words (crispy, soft, juicy, creamy). Conversation practice includes ordering food, expressing preferences ('I prefer...', 'I like... better than...'), and discussing daily meals.

sections.title: Healthy Eating and the Food Pyramid
sections.content: The food pyramid is a guide to balanced eating. The largest base shows foods to eat most: grains and cereals. Above that are fruits and vegetables. Next are protein foods and dairy. The smallest top shows foods to eat sparingly: fats, oils, and sweets. Students learn about nutrients: carbohydrates for energy, proteins for growth, vitamins and minerals for protection, and water for hydration. They discuss balanced diets and the consequences of malnutrition and overeating.

sections.title: Writing a Recipe
sections.content: Students learn the structure of a recipe: title, ingredients list with quantities, and step-by-step instructions. Imperative verbs are used: 'Cut', 'Mix', 'Boil', 'Stir', 'Add', 'Pour'. Transition words like 'first', 'then', 'next', 'after that', 'finally' organize the steps. Sample recipe: 'How to make vegetable khichuri'. Students also learn measurement vocabulary: a cup of, a teaspoon of, a pinch of, 200 grams of.

sections.title: Grammar: Conditional Sentences
sections.content: Conditional sentences (if-clauses) express conditions and results. Type 1 (real/possible): If + present simple, will + base verb. Example: 'If you eat too much junk food, you will gain weight.' Type 2 (unreal/hypothetical): If + past simple, would + base verb. Example: 'If I were a chef, I would cook healthy meals.' Students practice forming and using conditionals in the context of food, health, and daily choices.
